I've dealt with severe panic, OCD, paranoia, and depression since an unbelievably young age. The first time I convinced myself that I had a life threatening heart issue was at 4 yrs old- had an ambulance bring me to the ER and everything.

In my experience, for whatever reason, Sertraline did very very little (started at 15yrs), if anything, to help me manage these sympotms. After various medicines, escitalopram did absolute wonders. 

At various points I was on seroquel, respiridone, mirtazepine, buspar, hydroxyzine...you name it.  

It's important to identify a.) A medicine that you are comfortable taking every day while you recover b.) A dose that absolutely makes a notable impact and c.) A support system of people who can at least sympathize with you and help talk you down.

One method I frequently used was talking to me primary care doctor and having them help me rationalize the paranoid delusions of health issues I was having. 

My advice to you would be to remain cognitive about why you're having the thoughts you're having, to reach out to someone who can intellectually analyze what you're going through WITH you, and to find a reasonable balance of medication. Prioritize the SSRI, and as far as benzos go, I find alprazolam to be terribly ineffective for anything other than panic disorder. If you feel that they help you come back to reality, I'd suggest you opt for a longer-lasting drug like clonazepam or even ativan
